description: A single-panel table rendered as an image, described by the caption as the "Definition of texture component illustrated in Fig. 7". The table has five columns — Component, Symbol, Miller indices, Euler angles (φ1, Φ, φ2), Fiber — and nine rows, one per texture component. Each row pairs a component name with the plotting marker used for it: Brass (B) open diamond, Goss (G) filled diamond, Rotated Goss (RtG) open hexagon, Cube (C) open square, E open downward triangle, F filled downward triangle, Copper (Cu) open upward triangle, CopperTwin (CuT) filled upward triangle and S open circle. Miller indices and Euler-angle triplets (in degrees) are given for every component, e.g. Brass {110}⟨112⟩ at [55, 90, 45] and Goss {110}⟨001⟩ at [90, 90, 45]; E and F each carry two Euler-angle triplets. Fiber assignments are α and β (Brass), α and τ (Goss), α (RtG), γ (E, F), β and τ (Cu), τ (CuT), β (S); Cube shows "–", i.e. no fiber. The caption defines α-fiber as <110> parallel to ND, γ-fiber as <111> parallel to ND and τ-fiber as <110> parallel to TD. The panel is a legend/key rather than a data plot: it supplies the symbol-to-orientation mapping needed to read the texture (pole figure/ODF) measurements. No curves, maps or plotted data values appear.
measured_quantities: texture fiber designation (α, β, γ, τ)

observations.observation: The figure is a five-column table headed Component, Symbol, Miller indices, Euler angles (φ1, Φ, φ2), Fiber.
Nine texture components are tabulated: Brass (B), Goss (G), Rotated Goss (RtG), Cube (C), E, F, Copper (Cu), CopperTwin (CuT) and S.

The Symbol column shows geometric markers: open diamond for Brass (B), filled diamond for Goss (G), open hexagon for Rotated Goss (RtG), open square for Cube (C), open downward triangle for E, filled downward triangle for F, open upward triangle for Copper (Cu), filled upward triangle for CopperTwin (CuT) and open circle for S.
Brass (B) is listed as {110}⟨112⟩ with Euler angles [55, 90, 45] and assigned to the α and β fibers.
Goss (G) is listed as {110}⟨001⟩ with Euler angles [90, 90, 45] and assigned to the α and τ fibers.
Rotated Goss (RtG) is listed as {110}<110> with Euler angles [0, 90, 45] and assigned to the α fiber.
Cube (C) is listed as {001}⟨100⟩ with Euler angles [45, 0, 45] and shows '–' in the Fiber column, i.e. no fiber assignment.
E is listed as {111}<110> with two Euler angle triplets, [0, 55, 45] and [60, 55, 45], and belongs to the γ fiber.
F is listed as {111}<112> with two Euler angle triplets, [30, 55, 45] and [90, 55, 45], and belongs to the γ fiber.
All Euler angles are given as three-number triplets (φ1, Φ, φ2) without printed degree symbols inside the table; the column header contains no unit annotation.
The caption states the table defines the texture components illustrated in Fig. 7.
The caption states α-fiber is <110> parallel to ND, γ-fiber is <111> parallel to ND, and τ-fiber is <110> parallel to TD.
The image contains no plotted data, curves, colour maps or scale bars; it functions purely as a symbol/orientation key for texture figures.
